verdict.line: You lose if you let Mini Gnar poke you down at 1100 range for free; you win if you force a fight the moment he's committed as Mega Gnar.

brief.thesis: This matchup is a form check: Mini Gnar outranges your 900-range Q and punishes approach with his boomerang and Hyper-stacked autos, but Mega Gnar trades his Hop's bounce-distance and ranged Q for a melee-only Wallop stun and a committed body. OP.GG's 49.5% win rate over 186 games and an EVEN lane rating reflect that this is decided by which form Gnar is in when the fight starts, not by raw stats. Your solo-kill edge exists specifically because Tahm punishes the all-in Mega Gnar is forced into once he transforms.

theirWindow.when: Mini Gnar poking at max Q range
theirWindow.what: Don't walk up into his 1100-range Boomerang Throw or his Hyper-stacked auto for free damage. Hold at the edge of your own Q (900 range) and let him burn his Q cooldown (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s) on minions or whiffs before you commit.

yourWindow.when: Gnar transforms into Mega Gnar mid-trade
yourWindow.what: Mega Gnar loses Hop's bounce-extended range and his ranged Q becomes a stopping Boulder Toss, so he's stuck fighting at melee. Land your Q (Tongue Lash) stacks to build toward the 3-stack stun, then follow with W (Abyssal Dive) to knock him up and all-in before his W (Wallop) stun window opens.

start.why: 84.2% pick rate and the highest-sampled start (45.7% over 197 games); the passive block and regen directly counter Gnar's poke-based Boomerang Throw and auto harass while you're still out of Q range.

boots.why: 63.8% pick rate and the stronger winrate option (46.1% over 141 games); Gnar's Hyper passive and base autos are physical, and Steelcaps directly cuts the sustained auto-trading he relies on as Mini Gnar.

core.why: Stacks raw health, which directly scales both your passive (An Acquired Taste) bonus damage and your E (Thick Skin) stored-damage heal — the exact stat Gnar's kit doesn't threaten well.
Follows the measured build path into mid-game; keeps your health and resists climbing while Gnar's damage stays physical-only.
60% win rate over 15 games on this exact path; punishes Gnar's auto-attack-reliant Hyper passive and Mini Gnar's poke pattern directly with the reflect and grievous wounds.

runes.keystoneWhy: Every proc converts your total health into bonus damage and a heal, reinforcing the exact stat (health) that both your passive and E scale off — it rewards trading autos into Gnar's poke instead of trying to out-range him.

summoners.why: 50.5% win rate at 48.5% pick, the most-run combo; Ignite converts your solo-kill edge into an actual kill the moment Gnar transforms and loses his Hop escape.

playing.title: Don't chase Mini Gnar
playing.detail: His Boomerang Throw (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown) outranges your Q by 200 units. Walking up to trade autos into his Hyper passive just feeds his Rage bar faster.

playing.title: Stack Q for the stun, not the heal
playing.detail: Tongue Lash applies a stack of An Acquired Taste on every hit; at 3 stacks the next Q stuns and consumes them. Land it when he's forced to approach, not from max range.

playing.title: Hold W for the commitment
playing.detail: Abyssal Dive (21/20/19/18/17s cooldown) is your only gap closer with a knockup. Save it for the moment Gnar transforms rather than using it to answer early poke.

playing.title: Respect Mega Gnar's W once it's up
playing.detail: Wallop stuns in an area in front of him at melee range. Don't walk into his face immediately after he transforms — bait the stun on a minion or wait it out before committing your all-in.

playing.title: Track his ultimate rank
playing.detail: GNAR! drops to a 0-second cooldown at rank 4-5, meaning once he hits late game the only gate on repeated Mega transformations is his Rage bar, not the ability itself.

playing.title: Use R to answer burst, not to start fights
playing.detail: Devour has no base cooldown and can shield an ally or hit an enemy at 3 stacks; hold it to save yourself or a diving ally rather than opening with it.

playing.title: Farm through his poke if behind
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read on this lane is correct: if you can't force the Mega Gnar window, prioritize safe CS over contesting his max-range Boomerang Throw.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and the 49.5% head-to-head win rate over 186 games are measured from current-patch OP.GG data; the ability readings and trade-window judgment are my own analysis of the kit.

stats.opponentTip: If Gnar steps in your range, use [Q] to close in and fight him, but keep in mind that his (W) and (Q) make it difficult to kill him. Focus on farming instead or try to kill him when he is Mega Gnar.
